items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: Oh, Buddy P.T. played over on the boat? Yeah, Buddy, yeah. On the boat, yeah. That's when it was Buddy. Buddy. That's the gang I played with today.

ctx.x: I just remember. Well, that's all right. Buddy P.T. Buddy P.T. was played. Oh, Buddy P.T. played over on the boat? Yeah, Buddy, yeah. On the boat, yeah. That's when it was Buddy. Buddy. That's the gang I played with today. But I didn't know him. I just met him by me coming on a trip down here. And then I stayed here until she got well. She went back on a boat. Then, uh, that's where I met Lawrence Toker. Lawrence. Lawrence come to get her. To get some musician for him to go over to Mandeville or somewhere over…
I want to ask about that band in Birmingham. What was the name of it again?

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: Who was the leader? Well, Buddy P.T. was the leader. He played trumpet at that time.

ctx.x: So who was in that band with Johnny and all that?

Let me see. Nothing I remember. Let's see. I couldn't remember. Ivory Garner for Pre-Sax. Ain't that what his name? Oh my God. He was playing sax, Chinese. Now them's only two. Let me see. Who else can I think of? Who was the leader? Well, Buddy P.T. was the leader. He played trumpet at that time. He was a trumpet player. That's the only thing I can remember. Buddy and Ivory Garner and Chinese. Them's only one of them.
Them's only one of the bands who played bass?
